findings.failing_input: Race: hydrate's first-time-migration push (line 387) bumps pendingKeys but if that postWithRetry fails twice, the catch block at 298-302 decrements pendingKeys via 'prev.pendingKeys - 1' — but the success path bumps lastSyncAt via Date.now() inside the updater while the message uses lastError === null. Status transitions to 'error' but lastSyncAt is never updated for failed migration pushes. UI may show stale lastSyncAt next to error label, suggesting last sync was recent when it actually failed.
findings.expected: On final failure, lastSyncAt should remain the last successful sync (currently behavior); but UI consumers may misread.
findings.actual: lastSyncAt frozen at prior success; lastError set; user may not realize how stale lastSyncAt is.
findings.fix_sketch: Document UI contract: lastSyncAt = last SUCCESSFUL sync; render 'last sync at X (Y ago)' alongside error chip.
findings.regression_test_idea: Stub fetch to fail twice; assert syncState.lastError !== null AND syncState.lastSyncAt === prior value.

findings.failing_input: pushCloudKey called twice in rapid succession with different values: 1st push schedules retry on failure (pendingRetries[cloudKey] set); 2nd push within debounce window: !pendingTimers[localStorageKey] FALSE (timer still pending from 1st), so we don't +1; existingRetry exists, so we -1. Net: pendingKeys decremented from prior +1 but the 2nd push value will be sent. Counter could go to 0 prematurely if 1st push +1 was already cleared by an earlier failure decrement that happened between push 1 and push 2.
findings.expected: pendingKeys never goes negative (Math.max guards it) but can drift downward, causing premature 'ok' status.
findings.actual: Math.max(0, ...) prevents negative but masks drift; semantic counter is fuzzy.
findings.fix_sketch: Track a Set<string> of pending keys instead of a counter; pendingKeys = set.size. Idempotent add/delete.
findings.regression_test_idea: Stub fetch to fail twice for key A, then 2nd pushCloudKey(A) before retry; assert pendingKeys is consistent with actual in-flight POSTs.

findings.failing_input: localStorage value '5000.5e' (mistyped) — JSON.parse fails, Number('5000.5e') → NaN → not finite → returns raw string. Cloud sees a number-keyed slot receiving the string, may serialize back as string.
findings.expected: Cleaner: return null for unparseable goal values.
findings.actual: Returns the raw string, which gets POSTed as-is and could cause server-side parsing issues.
findings.fix_sketch: Add zod-style validation per-key in readLocal; for monthly-revenue-goal, parseFloat strict; if NaN return null.
findings.regression_test_idea: Set localStorage to invalid number string; call readLocal; assert null.
